subject: Request for penetration test artifacts and remediation status (NovaLabs incident follow-up)
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novalabs.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novalabs.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for penetration test report following 2026-04-09 service disruption

Evelyn,

We had an internal audit call this morning at NovaLabs after the service degradation on 2026-04-09 that impacted our integration. Our security team is asking for Redwood's most recent penetration test report (full findings) and an up-to-date remediation tracker.

Our auditors are treating this as an elevated item given the outage and want to review the details as part of our vendor risk assessment. Specifically we need:
- The latest penetration test report PDF (not just an executive summary)
- A column-by-column remediation status (timeline and owners)
- Any incident-adjacent notes that explain whether findings could be related to the outage on 4/9

Please let us know if you can provide the full report directly or if we need to sign an NDA or follow a formal evidence request flow. We need an initial response today if possible; auditors expect something by EOD PT.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Senior Information Security Manager
NovaLabs
maya.singh@novalabs.com
+1 415 555 0123
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report following 2026-04-09 service disruption

Maya — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the disruption on Friday. We're pulling the relevant artifacts now.

Quick answers up front:
- We'll provide a redacted penetration test summary and our current remediation tracker by end of day tomorrow.
- For the unredacted full report we typically require a standard evidence-request NDA (covers third-party artifacts and exploit details). I can route that to you now if you'd like.
- I will loop in our security lead (Neha) to confirm any linkage between the findings and the 4/9 incident.

Marcus — can you own coordinating the NDA and sending the redacted summary?
Neha — can you review whether any findings overlap with the root cause of Friday's outage and add notes to the tracker?

We'll be in touch with the files.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novalabs.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novalabs.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report following 2026-04-09 service disruption

Thanks, Evelyn.

A few clarifying points from our audit desk:
- NovaLabs requires the unredacted testing evidence for vendor critical services when an incident occurs that could affect confidentiality or integrity. The auditors will accept an NDA, but they also want confirmation that the remediation tracker maps to each CVE/issue (ID + status + verification evidence).
- If redactions are required for third-party proofs or exploit POCs, we need an exception approval flow or a point-of-contact to request the unredacted sections under controlled conditions.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. If you can send the redacted summary and the tracker first, we can start our internal review while the NDA is processed.

Best,
Maya
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novalabs.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report following 2026-04-09 service disruption

Maya — attaching a redacted penetration test summary and our current remediation tracker. See attachments: redwood_pen_test_summary-redacted.pdf (redactions limited to exploit POCs and third-party vendor findings) and remediation_tracker_novalabs.xlsx.

Notes from our internal review:
- We do not believe the 4/9 outage was caused by any of the findings called out in this test. The outage was traced to a resource scheduler regression that caused a throttling cascade; that root cause is unrelated to the pen-test findings.
- The remediation tracker maps each finding to a remediation owner and includes dates for mitigation and verification. Evidence columns include links to internal PRs and verification test runs; we can share those under an NDA.
- For full unredacted artifacts: we need a signed NDA and a signed handling agreement (standard for full test results). Once we have that, we can provide the full PDF and live evidence bundle.

If your auditors require an expedited path, Marcus can send the DocuSign NDA and we can share the unredacted files once countersigned.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com

Attachments: redwood_pen_test_summary-redacted.pdf (attachment), remediation_tracker_novalabs.xlsx (attachment)

Thank you, Neha — we received the redacted summary and the tracker and have started our internal review. A couple of items:
- The auditors pushed back that the redactions obscure some timeline details and exploit traces they consider important for root-cause attribution. They are explicitly requesting an unredacted copy under a vaulting agreement.
- NovaLabs is prepared to sign the standard NDA and a short handling addendum. Can Marcus send the NDA link and expected turnaround? We can get this signed today from our side.

Given the regulatory window, time is tight — appreciate any acceleration.

Maya
